## How they got there
Paris Saint-Germain reached the final by defeating Arsenal on penalties in a 1-1 draw, winning 4-3 on spot-kicks. Their path was defined by an attacking profile where they recorded 14.9 shots per game to beat 100% of teams in the group phase and 671 passes per game to outperform every other side in that same period. This dominance extended to possession, where a value of 64.0% allowed them to finish ahead of all competitors during the league stage.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would not have selected Paris Saint-Germain as its primary choice, ranking them fourth among knockout teams despite their status as a leading contender outside the top two. With a calculated probability of 16.1% to reach the final, they exceeded the base rate of 8.3% for random teams but fell short of the model's highest expectations. Consequently, the stage nearest to the model's expectation was the semi-finals, reflecting an anticipated performance level below their actual victory.

## Weak spots
The team displayed clear deficiencies in long-range distribution and physical output, recording only 8.6% of passes as long balls to beat just 8% of teams in the season. Additionally, they covered a distance of 114.5 km per game, a figure that placed them ahead of only 28% of their peers during the group phase. These areas represented the fewest beaten statistics for the squad, highlighting specific tactical and physical gaps compared to the rest of the competition.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Teams beaten (%)' figures say how many teams the club did better than on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where doing better means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Use 'significant' or 'significantly' only for a Holm-adjusted p-value comparison, never for other differences. Write plain markdown without tables.
